mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced interest rates lower the discount rate for equity valuations and increase the relative attractiveness of equities versus fixed income.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of all instances, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3.5% within the last month signals monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is not negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25% in the last month) and the unemployment rate falls (UNRATE decrease > 0.1pp in the last month), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, as the combination signals a strong economy without immediate recession risk, leading to robust corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 1 month AND UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of instances where both conditions are met, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market downturn (HOUST < 2000 in the last month), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns, as the decline in housing starts signals potential Fed rate cuts to stimulate the economy, which boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST < 2000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000 (thousands) in the last month, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns, as the decline signals potential Fed rate cuts to stimulate the economy, which boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST < 2000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

failure_condition: The 20-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of all instances, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5.0% in the last month, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns, as a low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market and robust economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return direction is not positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns, as the combination signals aggressive Fed policy that reduces liquidity and increases risk aversion, leading to equity market sell-offs.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return direction is not negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% AND FEDFUNDS rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
